why: A batch that fixes gates is the one where a green suite proves least: the gate can go back to being blind and every product test still passes, because the product did not change. So most of these put a gate back the way it was, and the rest make it wrong in the other direction — over-reporting, which is worse, because every later batch is measured by the number.

mutants.why: the exact state the batch found: the rule reports zero and the tree holds 104. Nothing else in the suite notices, because the product is unchanged and a gate is green when it sees nothing

the lazy fix, and the one a hurried session reaches for: it does find the tag at end of line, and it also calls <buttonBar> and <inputGroup> raw controls. A gate that over-reports is worse than one that under-reports, because a batch measured by it burns down things that were never wrong
back to 13, with eleven catches in six files invisible. The measure is named for route bodies that keep a try; counting a helper's name is how it stopped meaning that

two of the six hand-rollers disappear: mission-categories answers through api-response's serverError(), and memory/hindsight writes `status: isHindsightConnectionError(error) ? 503 : 500`. The second is the catch app-04b has already ruled stays hand-rolled forever, so it is the last one this measure should be blind to

each catch body becomes the whole rest of the file, so a route whose catch merely logs is counted because some LATER catch answers 500. That is exactly the pairing the brace matcher exists to prevent, and it makes the number bigger, which is the direction nobody checks
the sixteen documents outside docs/ go unchecked again, which is the state in which a move broke three of their links and nothing said so
the widened gate is only worth having if it fails on the thing it was widened to find. A stale link in a legal document reads as verified, which is worse than no link
scripts/ goes back to being the one tree that referees every batch and is measured by none of them; c0's own claim is that every declared measure is baselined, and this is the half that declares it
the other half: the key survives and reads zero, which is the shape a measure takes when it is quietly switched off rather than removed, and the one a reader is least likely to question

the first cut of this measure did exactly that, and the independent review caught it: counting only .ts/.tsx/.css/.mjs leaves 3,501 lines of shell, .mts, .cjs and Python out of a measure named for the tree they live in. A number that is 30 per cent short is the defect this batch exists to fix, wearing the batch's own clothes
